title: Applied Commerce Competency Framework
purpose: A deterministic curriculum-to-evidence layer for BIS. It defines what a learner may be shown to be progressing in, what evidence can support that statement, and what the system must not infer.
sourceBasis: Applied Commerce Grades 8–12 canonical learner books
Applied Commerce Assessment Checkpoint Guide · 4 October 2026
BIS canonical evidence classes and nine-stage Lab architecture

externalAlignment.statement: This framework is derived from Applied Commerce source material. It is not itself an official DBE assessment instrument, CAPS certification, qualification framework, or psychometric model.
externalAlignment.futureWork: Any external competency-framework crosswalk must be separately source-verified and versioned.

progressionModel.rule: Never collapse a learner into one global maturity score. Progression is reported per competency and only to the highest level supported by traceable evidence.

levels.label: Not yet evidenced
levels.meaning: The available record does not support a statement about this competency.

levels.label: Notices
levels.meaning: Identifies or observes a relevant pattern, feature, condition or distinction.

levels.label: Explains
levels.meaning: Explains the concept, relationship, reasoning or limitation in a way that can be reviewed.

levels.label: Applies
levels.meaning: Uses the concept in a task, plan, simulation or authentic situation.
minimumEvidence: PLAN or OUTCOME or governed task evidence
levels.boundary: Simulation supports application-under-conditions, not proof that a real-world action occurred.

levels.label: Tests and revises
levels.meaning: Makes a prediction or plan, gathers evidence, compares what happened and makes a justified revision.

levels.label: Transfers
levels.meaning: Adapts the competency to a meaningfully different context and explains what carries over, what changes and what remains uncertain.
levels.boundary: One transfer task is evidence of demonstrated transfer in that task, not permanent mastery.

criteria.label: Purpose and understanding
criteria.question: What are you trying to do, and why?

criteria.label: Evidence and assumptions
criteria.question: What supports this claim, and what remains uncertain?

criteria.label: Reasoning and choices
criteria.question: Why this choice rather than another?

criteria.label: Action and adaptation
criteria.question: What happened, and what changed because of it?

criteria.label: Communication and review
criteria.question: Can another reader follow your next step and limitation?

commonPortfolioRubric.warning: Rubric scores concern reviewed work. They do not measure learner worth, wealth, personality, future success or permanent capability.

competencies.title: Self-knowledge and identity
competencies.definition: Recognises how beliefs, values, experience and repeated action shape self-understanding without turning a single response into a fixed identity label.

competencies.title: Agency and initiative
competencies.definition: Identifies what is within reach, takes purposeful action, and adapts when permission, systems or first attempts do not produce the intended result.

competencies.title: Evidence and accurate thinking
competencies.definition: Separates observation from assumption, records traceable evidence, tests claims and states uncertainty or limits.

competencies.title: Behaviour change and self-management
competencies.definition: Observes repeated behaviour, designs manageable changes, follows through, recovers from setbacks and revises the method using evidence.

competencies.title: Goals, planning and prioritisation
competencies.definition: Turns intentions into specific priorities, sequences, schedules, first actions and review points while recognising trade-offs.

competencies.title: Decision and judgement
competencies.definition: Compares alternatives, consequences, constraints and trade-offs; explains why one choice is preferred and what could change the decision.

competencies.title: Value creation and enterprise
competencies.definition: Identifies needs, connects skills and resources to useful solutions, tests value propositions and learns from customer or market evidence.

competencies.title: Financial capability and resource stewardship
competencies.definition: Tracks, plans and reasons about money and other resources, including spending, saving, income, investment, debt and protection.

competencies.title: Systems and strategic thinking
competencies.definition: Maps connected parts, feedback, dependencies and leverage points; predicts ripple effects and redesigns weak systems.

competencies.title: Risk, resilience and protection
competencies.definition: Identifies uncertainty, capacity, downside, support and failure signals; prepares responses and revises plans after tests or setbacks.

competencies.title: Communication, influence and negotiation
competencies.definition: Communicates purpose and value clearly, listens, asks useful questions, negotiates responsibly and recognises social influence.

competencies.title: Collaboration, leadership and ethical responsibility
competencies.definition: Works with others, leads self and teams, considers people affected by decisions, and takes responsibility for delegated or amplified action.

competencies.title: Career and life navigation
competencies.definition: Builds and revises realistic pathways through learning, work, enterprise and adult transitions using evidence, relationships and next actions.

competencies.title: Long-term thinking, leverage and legacy
competencies.definition: Reasons across longer horizons, compounding effects and leverage; balances present action with future consequences and responsibility.

competencies.title: Transfer, reflection and meta-learning
competencies.definition: Reviews evidence, names what changed, carries learning into a different context and identifies the next question or practice need.
